Research

November 17, 2026

Assessing GPT-6.2 Astra Against Offensive Security Benchmarks

We evaluated GPT-6.2 Astra across FrontierCyber and CyScenarioBench. The model found and exploited new zero-day vulnerabilities in widely used targets, including a permission bypass in a popular mobile operating system. It solved 68 of 217 FrontierCyber challenges and completed 9 of 11 CyScenarioBench scenarios at least once, with a 63% average success rate. We observed no successful attacks on fully hardened targets.

October 28, 2026

GLM-5.3: Multi-Stage Cyber Operations and Instruction Violations

This publication evaluates GLM-5.3, Zhipu AI’s open-weight model, on CyScenarioBench. The model refused none of the tested offensive tasks and completed 3 of 13 multi-stage scenarios end to end, the strongest result we have recorded from an open-weight model. In a separate instruction-adherence evaluation, GLM-5.3 repeatedly reached correct answers by reproducing memorized code it was explicitly told not to use. The findings highlight the need for evaluations that check instruction compliance alongside answer correctness.

October 16, 2026

Assessing Reflection’s Beam Against Offensive Security Benchmarks

Reflection evaluated Beam, its first open-weight model, using Irregular’s offensive security benchmarks ahead of release. The model solved well-scoped individual security tasks on the Atomic Tasks suite but did not complete any end-to-end scenario on CyScenarioBench. The findings reinforce the importance of scenario-level evaluations for understanding how discrete capabilities translate into operational risk.

October 5, 2026

Containment Challenges: Testing the Boundaries of Cyber Evaluations

Containment challenges turn a frontier model's capabilities against the security boundaries of its own evaluation environment before the capability evaluation begins. Each challenge tests the full planned configuration, including the harness, tools, permissions, resource limits, and infrastructure connections. Each challenge gives the model an explicit objective to cross a defined security boundary, with a verifiable success condition and room to develop its own approach. The results help evaluators assess containment, investigate findings, and retest controls before capability evaluations begin.

Assessing Claude Opus 5.5 Against Offensive Security Benchmarks

Anthropic used CyScenarioBench, Irregular's benchmark for multi-stage offensive cyber operations, in its cyber evaluations of Claude Opus 5.5. Across a ten-challenge subset, Claude Opus 5.5 raised the average solve rate by roughly 28% over Claude Opus 5 and by more than an order of magnitude over Claude Sonnet 5, while moving ahead of Claude Mythos 5.1.

September 16, 2026

Agentic Self-Modification in Open-Weights Systems

In controlled experiments, a coding agent given a routine software-maintenance task fine-tuned and replaced the open-weights model powering both the application it was maintaining and future instances of itself. It was never instructed to train, modify weights, or deploy a replacement. This research identifies the environmental conditions that make model modification more likely, demonstrates that agent-initiated training can embed recoverable information and remove learned refusals, and sets out the controls needed where agents have access to weights, training tools, and a deployment path.

Assessing GPT-6 Astra: FrontierCyber Measures a Sharp Increase in Cyber Capability

We evaluated GPT-6 Astra across FrontierCyber, CyScenarioBench, and our Atomic Challenges. On FrontierCyber, the model solved more than twice as many challenges as GPT-5.6 Sol and discovered multiple previously unknown vulnerabilities in widely deployed software and mobile systems. It also more than doubled the average success rate on CyScenarioBench. Neither model solved an Elite FrontierCyber challenge, and we did not observe successful attacks against fully hardened targets.

September 3, 2026

Introducing SOLVE+: Scoring Cyber Scenarios (Version 0.5)

SOLVE+ extends Irregular's SOLVE difficulty-scoring framework from vulnerabilities research and exploit to the full scope of an offensive cyber operation, adding four capabilities, and is built to score full multi-step scenarios rather than single-capability atomic tasks. Each step in a scenario receives its own capability scores, which aggregate into a scenario score for the operation as a whole, localizing where difficulty sits rather than averaging it. Because difficulty is measured against human skill levels, a score also serves as an estimate of the uplift a model provides to its operator.

August 19, 2026

Assessing Kimi K3 Against Offensive Security Benchmarks

This publication describes Irregular’s evaluation of Kimi K3 across Atomic Tasks, CyScenarioBench, and FrontierCyber. Kimi K3 became the first open-weight model Irregular evaluated to solve CyScenarioBench challenges, demonstrating a meaningful improvement in long-horizon operational reliability over previous open-weight models. It produced no verified FrontierCyber solves, but its overall performance suggests that open-weight models are following the closed frontier’s cyber capability trajectory on a short delay.
